newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope appoints "commissar" to run troubled order.
newsitem.headline: Pope appoints "commissar" to run troubled order.

text.p: Pope John Paul on Friday appointed a personal representative to temporarily oversee the running of a well-known religious order of priests whose magazines have sometimes questioned official Church teachings.
The Society of St Paul publishes Italy's largest-selling weekly, Famiglia Cristiana (Christian Family) and other widely circulated magazines. It also publishes religious magazines and books abroad.
The order has been plagued by internal rows among its Italian leaders over the future direction of its multi-million dollar religious publishing and television concerns.
Recently some of the articles in the magazines and books published by the order have indirectly questioned some Roman Catholic teachings on sexual ethics and other issues.
The Vatican said the Pope's personal delegate, effectively a commissar, would take over the main functions of the order's superior general until the election of a new leader can be held.
The delegate is Bishop Antonio Buoncristiani.

The Pope took similar action with the Jesuits in the early 1980s. He appointed a personal delegate who ran the order until the election of a new leader who was more in tune with the Pope's conservative thinking on social justice issues.
